stories.headline: FDA approves first pan-RAS pill for pancreatic cancer, nearly doubling survival to 13.2 months

key_facts.fact: On August 26, 2026 the FDA approved Revolution Medicines' RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have had at least one prior systemic therapy or cannot take multiagent chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: On August 26, 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial of 500 patients, median overall survival was 13.2 months with daraxonrasib versus 6.7 months with chemotherapy (HR 0.40, P<.0001); median progression-free survival was 7.2 vs 3.6 months and response rate 30% vs 11%.
key_facts.excerpt: median overall survival was 13.2 months ... in the daraxonrasib arm and 6.7 months ... in the standard of care arm (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.40 ... P < .0001). Median progression-free survival was 7.2 months ... and 3.6 months ... Objective response rate was 30% ... and 11%

key_facts.fact: The FDA cleared the drug roughly 6.5 months ahead of its user-fee goal date, using the Real-Time Oncology Review pilot and the Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher program.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved this application approximately 6.5 months ahead of the FDA goal date. This application is part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher (CNPV) pilot program

key_facts.fact: The once-daily tablet is already available in the US at a wholesale acquisition cost of $39,800 for a 30-day supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Once-daily oral RASONQUE tablets are now available in the United States, with a wholesale acquisition cost of $39,800 for a 30-day supply at the recommended daily dose.

key_facts.fact: Daraxonrasib blocks a mutated RAS protein that fuels tumour growth in more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases, an approach that eluded drugmakers for decades; five-year survival in pancreatic cancer is 13%, and 3% for late-stage disease.
key_facts.excerpt: FDA officials gave expedited approval to the first-of-a-kind pill, called daraxonrasib, which blocks a mutated protein that fuels tumor growth in more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases. It's an approach that previously eluded drugmakers for decades.

key_facts.fact: Angelo de Claro, director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, called the results 'unprecedented' in an area of high unmet need.
key_facts.excerpt: "This drug showed unprecedented results in an area of high unmet need," Angelo de Claro, director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, said in an agency announcement.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea hikes to 3% and lifts 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% on the semiconductor boom

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Board raised the base rate by 25 basis points to 3.00% from 2.75% on August 27, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Monetary Policy Decision (August 27, 2026) The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea decided today to raise the Base Rate by 25 basis points from 2.75% to 3.00%.

key_facts.fact: It is the second consecutive hike, the first back-to-back increase since January 2023, and takes the policy rate to its highest level since January 2025. Six of seven board members backed the move; Hwang Kun-il dissented in favour of holding at 2.75%.
key_facts.excerpt: It also marked the first back-to-back rate increases since January 2023 ... Six of the seven board members supported Thursday's rate hike. Hwang Kun-il dissented, proposing that the central bank leave the benchmark rate unchanged at 2.75 percent.

key_facts.fact: The BOK raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% from 2.6% and its 2027 forecast to 2.9% from 2.1%, citing a solid semiconductor cycle driving exports and investment.
key_facts.excerpt: The central bank forecast economic growth of 3.3 percent this year and 2.9 percent next year. That is up 0.7 percentage point and 0.8 percentage point, respectively, from its May projections of 2.6 percent for this year and 2.1 percent for next year.

key_facts.fact: Second-quarter real GDP grew 3.7% year-on-year against a 3.0% forecast, and gross domestic income rose 15.6% year-on-year, the fastest since Q1 1988, driven by AI-fuelled semiconductor demand and better terms of trade.
key_facts.excerpt: Real gross domestic product (GDP) grew 3.7% year-on-year, well above the Bank of Korea's 3.0% forecast ... The year-on-year increase in GDI ... reached 15.6% in the second quarter ... the highest since the first quarter of 1988. Surging demand for semiconductors, driven by expanded investment in artificial intelligence (AI)

key_facts.fact: Financial-stability risks also drove the decision: Seoul home transaction prices rose 1.1% in July and bank household loans grew 5.4 trillion won that month. Of 21 rate projections from board members for six months ahead, 16 pointed above the current 3.00%.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, Seoul home transaction prices rose 1.1 percent from the previous month ... Bank household loans increased by 5.4 trillion won in July ... Of a total 21 rate projections presented by members, 3.50 percent accounted for 6, 3.25 percent for 10, and the current level of 3.00 percent for 5.

key_facts.fact: Korea's July headline inflation eased to 2.8% but core inflation rose to 2.6%; the BOK kept its 2026 inflation forecast at 2.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: The July consumer inflation rate eased to 2.8 percent from the previous month, but core inflation excluding food and energy rose to 2.6 percent. The central bank forecast consumer inflation of 2.7 percent this year

stories.headline: Iran says it struck a deal with Oman to split the Strait of Hormuz and its revenues

key_facts.fact: On August 26 the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Iran and Oman had agreed on how to share the Strait of Hormuz's territory and its shipping revenues after about a month of talks.
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Iran and Oman had reached an agreement on their shares of the territory and revenues. "The Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and the country of Oman... We have been in negotiations with Oman for about a month"

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian source told Reuters the same day that the agreement 'has not been finalised' and that talks on the details were continuing.
key_facts.excerpt: "An agreement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz has not been finalised," the senior Iranian source told Reuters, adding that the talks were continuing on the details of an accord.

key_facts.fact: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the strait will not open unless the US ends its blockade of Iranian ports, pays compensation and removes sanctions; Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said it would not reopen to US vessels until Washington honours the June memorandum.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi cautioned, however, that the strait would not reopen to U.S. vessels until the United States follows through on its obligations under the June memorandum of understanding

key_facts.fact: The strait handled one-fifth of global oil and LNG shipments before the war began in February and remains largely shut; oil fell for a third straight day on August 26, dropping more than 1.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: the strait, which handled one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the war began in February ... Oil prices fell for a third day, dropping more than 1.5%, following signs of renewed efforts to seek a mediated end to the war

key_facts.fact: Also on August 26, Pakistani government sources said Islamabad has proposed a fresh 60-day window for the US and Iran to resume direct talks, after army chief Asim Munir carried a US offer to Tehran trading the strait's reopening for lifting 'a sizable part' of sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan is trying to broker a fresh 60-day period to reach a final agreement to end the months-long war between the US and Iran ... Pakistan's army chief also conveyed to the Iranian leadership the fresh US proposal seeking reopening of the strait in exchange for lifting of "a sizable part" of economic sanctions on Tehran

key_facts.fact: Trump warned Oman on August 17 against cooperating with Iran, telling Fox News: 'If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the shit out of them.'
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump has warned Oman against cooperating with Iran, telling Fox News on August 17: "If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the shit out of them."

key_facts.fact: Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi said the proposed corridor would route inbound commercial vessels through Iranian waters and outbound ships partly through Iranian and Omani waters, exclude military vessels, and last 30 to 60 days while a permanent traffic plan is negotiated.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the proposed arrangement, commercial vessels entering the Arabian Gulf would travel through Iranian waters, while outbound ships would follow a route passing partly through Iranian and Omani waters, Gharibabadi told state television late Tuesday. He said the routes would be temporary and that Tehran and Muscat would have 30 to 60 days to discuss a permanent maritime traffic plan.

stories.headline: Gaza envoy warns UN of a 'point of no return' as Hamas agrees for the first time to hand over weapons

key_facts.fact: Nickolay Mladenov, high representative for Gaza on Trump's Board of Peace, told the UN Security Council on August 26 that a collapse of the ceasefire process would be 'a point of no return for everyone.'
key_facts.excerpt: "no roadmap to return to, there will be no administration to deploy and there will be nothing left on the ground to rebuild. That would not be a setback. It would be a point of no return for everyone," Mladenov told the council.

key_facts.fact: Mladenov said that for the first time Hamas and the armed factions in Gaza have agreed to hand over their weapons and transfer full civilian and security authority to a UN-recognised transitional administration.
key_facts.excerpt: "For the first time, Hamas and the armed factions in Gaza have agreed to hand over their weapons and to transfer full governing authority -- civilian and security -- to a transitional administration recognized by the United Nations," Mladenov said.

key_facts.fact: The warning followed Netanyahu's public rejection of the 15-point US plan; he insists Hamas must be fully disarmed before any Israeli withdrawal, while Hamas wants a phased, reciprocal process.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the plan, saying Hamas must be fully disarmed before any Israeli withdrawal ... Hamas insists on a phased and reciprocal process, while Israel demands that disarmament be carried out first.

key_facts.fact: Gaza's Health Ministry says at least 1,288 Palestinians have been killed and 4,290 wounded since the US-brokered ceasefire took effect in October; the total toll since October 2023 stands at 73,422.
key_facts.excerpt: Gaza's Ministry of Health said at least 1,288 Palestinians have been killed and 4,290 wounded since a US-brokered "ceasefire" came into effect in October ... At least 73,422 Palestinians have been killed since

key_facts.fact: Palestinian UN ambassador Riyad Mansour told the Council that Israeli annexation moves, including new bidding tenders for the E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank, are killing prospects for regional peace.
key_facts.excerpt: Riyad Mansour, the Palestinian ambassador to the UN, told the Security Council that Israeli annexations of Palestinian land are killing prospects for regional peace. Noting the recent release of bidding tenders for the E1 settlement project

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu's hardline stance comes ahead of an Israeli election on October 27 and amid pressure from far-right coalition partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu's hardline position comes ahead of an Israeli election on Oct. 27 and amid mounting pressure from far-right coalition partners opposed to making concessions on Gaza.

stories.headline: Zelensky unveils a three-step US-Europe plan for a ceasefire and a buffer zone with Russia

key_facts.fact: On August 26 Zelensky said Ukraine, the US and European partners had drafted a set of proposals to end the war, worked out with Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
key_facts.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that, together with the United States and Europe, a set of proposals had been developed to end the war in Ukraine ... Kyiv has been working on the plan together with envoys of President Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and European officials.

key_facts.fact: The plan has three steps: a ceasefire, mutual withdrawal of Russian and Ukrainian troops from the front line, and the creation of a buffer zone.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan would provide for: - a ceasefire; - mutual withdrawal of Russian and Ukrainian troops from the front line; - the creation of a buffer zone.

key_facts.fact: The buffer zone would be a 'free economic zone' administered by a third party, with its manager still undecided; a third section would cover EU and NATO roles and security guarantees for Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Then a buffer "free economic zone" would be established and administered by a third party ... But Zelenskyy said it is still undecided who would manage this buffer zone. The third major section would detail the roles of the European Union and NATO, the provision of security guarantees for Ukraine

key_facts.fact: Moscow still demands Ukrainian withdrawal from all of Donbas and has shown no sign of dropping its maximalist territorial claims; Zelensky said no settlement should be expected for at least a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow continues to demand that Ukraine's forces withdraw from all of the Donbas and has signaled no inclination to abandon its other maximalist territorial claims. Zelenskiy has also said that the window for negotiations remains extended and that no settlement can be expected for at least a year.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine resumed drone attacks on Moscow overnight into August 26, hours after CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unannounced visit; Kyiv had agreed to a US request to pause strikes on the capital during the trip. At least 10 drones were downed near Moscow and Russia claimed 426 shot down nationwide.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine resumed drone attacks on Moscow overnight into Wednesday morning ... hours after the departure of the plane that carried CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow for an unannounced visit ... At least 10 drones were shot down while flying toward Moscow ... The drones intercepted over Moscow were among the 426 Ukrainian craft claimed shot down overnight by the Russian Defense Ministry.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Ukrainian forces hit 16 facilities in Russia in 24 hours, including oil facilities, airfields and a missile unit; Russia launched 162 drones at Ukraine, killing a woman and a four-year-old girl in the Chernihiv region.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said ... Ukrainian forces "targeted 16 facilities in Russia" over the previous 24 hours, including oil facilities, airfields and a missile unit ... Russia launched 162 drones into the country overnight ... a woman and a 4-year-old girl were killed in a Russian attack in the northern Chernihiv region

stories.headline: Shein prices Hong Kong IPO at $26.5bn, a 73% cut from its 2022 private peak

key_facts.fact: Shein is set to price its Hong Kong IPO at HK$48.56 a share, near the midpoint of the HK$47.60-HK$49.50 range, raising about HK$13.6 billion ($1.73 billion) and valuing the company at roughly $26.5 billion, sources told Reuters on August 27.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is set to price the deal at HK$48.56 a share, near the midpoint of its HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 range, the people said, raising about HK$13.6 billion ($1.73 billion).

key_facts.fact: The valuation is about a quarter of the nearly $100 billion peak Shein reached in private markets in 2022, and well below the $66 billion it secured in a 2023 round.
key_facts.excerpt: The valuation would be about one-quarter of the nearly $100 billion private market peak Shein reached in 2022, and well below the $66 billion valuation it secured in a 2023 fundraising round.

key_facts.fact: Shein had initially sought a $30-40 billion valuation when investor meetings began; it is selling about 280 million Class B shares and plans to start trading on September 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Shein had initially targeted a $30 billion to $40 billion valuation before investor meetings began ... The company is selling around 280 million Class B shares to institutional and retail investors ... Trading is set to begin September 1 on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

key_facts.fact: The deal is the largest new share sale in Hong Kong in 2026, surpassing autonomous-driving firm Momenta Global's $751 million offering in July. Cornerstone investors led by Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic subscribed for about $383 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Shein's IPO is the largest new share sale in Hong Kong in 2026, surpassing autonomous driving firm Momenta Global's US$751 million offering in July ... Cornerstone investors led by existing shareholders Boyu, Tiger Global and General Atlantic have subscribed for about US$383 million worth of Shein shares

key_facts.fact: Shein, headquartered in Singapore and founded in China, turned to Hong Kong after failed attempts to list in London and New York; it sells $5 dresses and $10 jeans in about 160 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Known for selling US$5 dresses and US$10 jeans to shoppers in about 160 countries, Shein had first sought an IPO valuation of US$30 billion to US$40 billion when investor meetings ahead of the IPO kicked off.

key_facts.fact: About 80% of the proceeds are earmarked for technology infrastructure, with the rest for global expansion; Shein has also agreed to pay up to $3.5 billion in cash to earlier private-round investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Shein plans to use about 80% of IPO proceeds to improve its technology infrastructure. The remaining funds will support expanding the brand's global reach and market presence. Shein has also agreed to pay up to $3.5 billion in cash to investors from earlier private funding rounds.

stories.headline: Brazil sues Discord for R$500 million over child-safety failures after a teen's death

key_facts.fact: Brazil's government filed a federal civil suit against Discord on August 26 seeking 500 million reais (about $97 million) in collective moral damages for failing to comply with laws protecting children and women, Solicitor General Jorge Messias said.
key_facts.excerpt: The Brazilian government has sued chat platform Discord, seeking 500 million reais ($97 million) through a civil collective moral damages lawsuit as it accuses the firm of failing to comply with laws protecting children and women, the country's solicitor general, Jorge Messias, said on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The suit asks the court to force Discord to fix its safety mechanisms, age-verification systems, parental controls, moderation and communication features, under a daily fine of 500,000 reais for non-compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: The lawsuit requests Discord to bring safety mechanisms, age-verification systems, parental supervision tools, content moderation practices and communication features into compliance, subject to a daily fine of 500,000 reais ($97,099).

key_facts.fact: The action follows the July suicide of a 13-year-old girl who was encouraged to kill herself during a Discord broadcast; five teenagers and an adult have been arrested. Brazil's data protection agency ANPD ordered Discord to suspend livestreams on August 12, and the company complied on August 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Brazil's National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) ordered Discord to suspend livestreams earlier this month after a 13-year-old girl was encouraged to kill herself during a broadcast ... The messaging platform, with over 90 million active daily users, agreed to suspend livestreaming in Brazil on August 17

key_facts.fact: The government said the lawsuit came after negotiations failed, with Discord's proposals 'deemed insufficient to eliminate the identified risks,' and said the platform 'continues to exhibit flaws in its age verification and user protection mechanisms.'
key_facts.excerpt: A government statement said the lawsuit was filed after failed negotiations with Discord whose proposals were "deemed insufficient to eliminate the identified risks."

key_facts.fact: Discord called the lawsuit disproportionate and said it does not accurately reflect its safety stance or compliance with Brazilian law, adding it had offered technical adjustments and a financial investment.
key_facts.excerpt: In a statement, Discord said the lawsuit is disproportionate and does not accurately reflect the company's stance regarding safety and compliance with the Brazilian law. Discord added it has presented the office of Brazil's solicitor general with a proposal to improve the safety of its operations in the country

key_facts.fact: The ANPD also fined TikTok $30 million on August 25, part of Brasilia's broader crackdown on platforms over child safety.
key_facts.excerpt: ANPD also fined TikTok $30 [million] on Tuesday for ... one of the more aggressive approach the Brazilian government has
